subject.title: fix(gateway): regenerate native hook descriptors when relay unavailable after restart

question: May pre-invocation native relay unavailability fall back to in-process `runBeforeToolCallHook`, or must restart recovery repair the relay identity while retaining fail-closed behavior?
rationale: Both paths affect the native tool-approval boundary, and source inspection cannot establish that every native-relay policy is equivalent to the proposed in-process fallback without explicit owner intent and live proof.

options.title: Repair relay identity
options.body: Refresh or regenerate the descriptor and generation at restart/resume so native enforcement remains the canonical path.

options.title: Approve narrow fallback
options.body: Permit only recognized pre-invocation unavailability to use local policy after live proof shows equivalent allow and deny behavior.

options.title: Pause this approach
options.body: Close or redesign this PR if current generation-persistence recovery already resolves the live restart failure without changing approval semantics.

recommendation.title: Repair relay identity
recommendation.body: Refresh or regenerate the descriptor and generation at restart/resume so native enforcement remains the canonical path.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the native relay and direct-bridge enforcement architecture whose fallback contract is being changed.
